title: Opportunities for Business, Jobs, Tourism and Leisure from Proposed Establishment of Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone
what_it_is: Opportunities for Business, Jobs, Tourism and Leisure from Proposed Establishment of Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone

sections.label: Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone
sections.summary: The proposed Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone could strengthen economic ties, with a task force studying collaboration and an update due at the 10th Singapore-Malaysia Leaders' Retreat.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The proposed Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone has the potential to strengthen the excellent economic relationship between Singapore and Johor.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: A special task force has been set up to study the broad areas of collaboration.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: We will provide an update on its progress at the 10th Singapore-Malaysia Leaders’ Retreat scheduled for later this year.

sections.label: JS-SEZ task force meeting
sections.summary: Singapore and Malaysia agreed to set up a task force to study the JS-SEZ, which will sit under the JMCIM and build on its workgroups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: This meeting was co-chaired by Singapore's Minister for National Development Desmond Lee and Malaysia's Minister of Economy Mohd Rafizi Ramli.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: It was agreed during the meeting between the two Ministers that Singapore and Malaysia would set up a task force to study the establishment of JS-SEZ to do a few things: one, to drive economic growth; two, to strengthen economic connectivity between Singapore and Johor; and three, to promote collaboration for the mutual benefit of both countries and our peoples.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I have explained that the JS-SEZ will sit under the auspices of the JMCIM.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: And if I could use the data-points since the COVID-19 measures were lifted, from January to June 2022, Singapore was Johor's second largest foreign investor after Japan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: During this period, Singapore contributed to around 70% of Johor's total foreign direct investment (FDI) in the manufacturing sector, with about 3.97 billion ringgit in investments, most of which come from investments in the electric and electronics and medical equipment sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: As I shared earlier, it is complementary so that we can anchor regional headquarters activities here, we can also anchor research and development (R&D) activities and supply chain management here, so that our Singaporean workers are well-placed to perform these functions, to help the companies manage, integrate, orchestrate their Pan-Asian operations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I want to assure the Member that the JS-SEZ will build on the foundation set by the various JMCIM workgroups to drive sustainable growth, develop human capital and improve infrastructure and connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The meeting just took place two weeks ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: We will certainly provide the House with an update on the JS-SEZ during the 10th Singapore-Malaysia Leaders' Retreat scheduled for later this year.
